MA-SPK-F00-Q01.text: Here's a number for you to read. Look at it, then say it out loud.

MA-SPK-F00-Q02.text: Count the apples out loud. Then say how many there are altogether.

MA-SPK-F00-Q03.text: What is one plus one? Work it out and say the answer.

MA-SPK-F00-Q04.text: Look at the number on your screen. What is it called? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-F00-Q05.text: Three plus two. Have a think, then say the answer out loud.

MA-SPK-F00-Q06.text: Count the stars on your screen out loud, then tell me how many there are.

MA-SPK-F00-Q07.text: Start at five and take away one. What number do you get? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-F00-Q08.text: Take a look at this number. When you know what it is, say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T01-Q01.text: Here's a number for you. Take a look at it on the screen, and when you're ready, say its name out loud.

MA-SPK-T01-Q02.text: There's a single number waiting on your screen. Have a good look, then say it clearly into the microphone.

MA-SPK-T01-Q03.text: Take a look at the number in front of you. What is it called? Say it out loud, nice and clearly.

MA-SPK-T01-Q04.text: Quick check: what number can you see on the screen? Say it out loud so I can hear it.

MA-SPK-T01-Q05.text: This number has two digits. Look at it closely, then say the whole number out loud.

MA-SPK-T01-Q06.text: Have a look at the number on your screen. Read it to yourself first, then say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T01-Q07.text: Let's read a number. Look at the screen, think about what it's called, and say it into the microphone.

MA-SPK-T01-Q08.text: Find the number on your screen. When you know its name, say it out loud, clearly and at your own pace.

MA-SPK-T01-Q09.text: A bigger number has appeared on your screen. Look at both digits, then say the whole number out loud, as if you're announcing it.

MA-SPK-T01-Q10.text: Imagine this number is painted on the front door of a house. What would you call it? Look closely and say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T02-Q01.text: Let's count some apples. Point to each apple as you go, count them out loud, and finish by saying how many there are.

MA-SPK-T02-Q02.text: Some socks are on your screen. Count them out loud, one by one, and say how many there are altogether.

MA-SPK-T02-Q03.text: How many cars can you see? Count them out loud, saying a number for each car, then tell me the total.

MA-SPK-T02-Q04.text: Time to count stars. Say a number for each star you see, and finish by saying how many there are.

MA-SPK-T02-Q05.text: There's a little group of fish on your screen. Count them out loud, slowly, so you don't miss any.

MA-SPK-T02-Q06.text: Count the balloons out loud. Work from left to right, so that each balloon gets counted just once.

MA-SPK-T02-Q07.text: Let's count coins, the way you might at a shop counter. Say each number out loud as you go, then the total.

MA-SPK-T02-Q08.text: Some puzzle pieces are waiting to be counted. Count them out loud, keeping your place as you go.

MA-SPK-T02-Q09.text: Buzz buzz, a busy group of bees has flown onto your screen. Can you count them all out loud without missing a single bee?

MA-SPK-T02-Q10.text: A flutter of butterflies has landed on your screen. Count them out loud, slowly, and tell me how many came to visit.

MA-SPK-T03-Q01.text: What do you get when you put two and three together? Work it out, then say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T03-Q02.text: Start with six and take away two. What's left? Say the answer out loud when you've got it.

MA-SPK-T03-Q03.text: Four plus four. Work it out in your head or on your fingers, then say the answer.

MA-SPK-T03-Q04.text: Here's a subtraction: nine take away five. Have a think, and say what you get.

MA-SPK-T03-Q05.text: Seven plus six. Take your time working it out, then say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T03-Q06.text: Fifteen take away eight. What does that leave? Work it out and say it clearly.

MA-SPK-T03-Q07.text: Try this sum: eight plus five. When you've worked it out, say the answer into the microphone.

MA-SPK-T03-Q08.text: Twelve minus seven. Work it out in whatever way suits you, then say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T03-Q09.text: Imagine you have seventeen marbles and you find six more. Work out seventeen plus six, then say the answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T03-Q10.text: Here's a puzzle for you: twenty-four take away nine. What do you get? Work it out, then say it nice and clearly.

MA-SPK-T04-Q01.text: Look at the number sentence on your screen. Read the whole thing out loud, saying each number and each symbol as you go.

MA-SPK-T04-Q02.text: Here's an equation to read. Say it out loud from left to right, the numbers and the signs too.

MA-SPK-T04-Q03.text: Your job this time is reading, not working out. Read the equation on the screen out loud, all the way to the end.

MA-SPK-T04-Q04.text: Can you read this equation out loud? Take it piece by piece: a number, a sign, a number, the equals sign, and the last number.

MA-SPK-T04-Q05.text: Have a look at the equation. When you're ready, read it out loud exactly as it's written.

MA-SPK-T04-Q06.text: Read this number sentence aloud. Go slowly, and say each symbol by its name.

MA-SPK-T04-Q07.text: Equations can be read just like sentences. Read the one on your screen out loud, from the first number to the last.

MA-SPK-T04-Q08.text: Let's practise reading maths out loud. Say the equation on your screen, every number and every sign.

MA-SPK-T04-Q09.text: This equation has some bigger numbers in it. Read it out loud like a sentence, nice and steady, all the way to the end.

MA-SPK-T04-Q10.text: This equation might look tricky, but you only need to read it. Say it out loud, piece by piece, numbers and signs.

MA-SPK-T05-Q01.text: There's a shape on your screen. Do you know what it's called? Say its name out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q02.text: Look at this shape carefully, at its sides and its corners. What's its name? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q03.text: Here's a shape to name. Count its corners if that helps, then say what it's called.

MA-SPK-T05-Q04.text: What shape can you see on the screen? Say the name of it out loud, clearly.

MA-SPK-T05-Q05.text: Have a look at this shape. Think about its sides, then say its name into the microphone.

MA-SPK-T05-Q06.text: This shape might remind you of something. What's its shape name? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q07.text: Take a look at the shape on your screen. When you know its name, say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q08.text: Here's a shape you may well know. What do we call it? Say its name out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q09.text: Ooh, a shape with lots of sides. Can you count them? Then say the name of this shape out loud.

MA-SPK-T05-Q10.text: Time for a shape hunt. Look at the sides and the corners, then say what this shape is called.

MA-SPK-T06-Q01.text: Here are two numbers, three and seven. Which is bigger, or which is smaller? Say it out loud in a sentence.

MA-SPK-T06-Q02.text: Compare five and two. Tell me which number is bigger, or which is smaller.

MA-SPK-T06-Q03.text: Think about one and nine. Which is the bigger number, or the smaller? Say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T06-Q04.text: Look at four and eight. Say which is bigger or which is smaller, using a full sentence.

MA-SPK-T06-Q05.text: Fourteen and eleven are on your screen. Which is bigger, or smaller? Have a think, then say it.

MA-SPK-T06-Q06.text: Careful, these two look alike: twenty-three and thirty-two. Which is bigger, or which is smaller? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T06-Q07.text: Picture two purses. One holds fifteen pence and the other holds nine pence. Which amount is bigger, or smaller? Say it in a sentence.

MA-SPK-T06-Q08.text: Seventeen and seventy-one look a bit alike. Which is bigger, or which is smaller? Tell me out loud.

MA-SPK-T06-Q09.text: Here's a puzzle: double six and double nine. Which is bigger, or which is smaller? Work it out and say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T06-Q10.text: Let's compare half of ten and a quarter of twenty. Work out each part first, then compare them and say what you find.

MA-SPK-T07-Q01.text: Let's count in twos, all the way up to ten. Say each number out loud as you go.

MA-SPK-T07-Q02.text: This time, count in fives up to twenty-five. Keep a steady rhythm and say each number out loud.

MA-SPK-T07-Q03.text: Can you count in tens, up to fifty? Say each number clearly as you go.

MA-SPK-T07-Q04.text: Try counting in threes until you reach fifteen. Take your time, and say every number out loud.

MA-SPK-T07-Q05.text: Count in fours up to twenty. It's fine to go slowly; just say each number out loud.

MA-SPK-T07-Q06.text: Here's a twist: count backwards in fives, starting at thirty. Say each number out loud as you go down.

MA-SPK-T07-Q07.text: Count in sixes all the way up to thirty. Say each number out loud, nice and steady.

MA-SPK-T07-Q08.text: Imagine a bag with eight shoes inside. Count them as pairs, in twos, saying each number out loud.

MA-SPK-T07-Q09.text: Ready for bigger jumps? Count in sevens up to thirty-five, saying each number out loud like footsteps along a path.

MA-SPK-T07-Q10.text: Let's go exploring in nines. Count in nines up to forty-five, and say each stop along the way out loud.

MA-SPK-T08-Q01.text: Look at the apples on your screen. Tell me about them using a number. You might say how many there are, or something else you notice.

MA-SPK-T08-Q02.text: Here are some cars. Describe what you see, and make sure you use a number in your sentence.

MA-SPK-T08-Q03.text: Can you describe these stars in a sentence that has a number in it? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T08-Q04.text: Some socks are on your screen. Talk about them using a number. Any true sentence will do.

MA-SPK-T08-Q05.text: Have a look at the coins. Say a sentence about them that includes a number.

MA-SPK-T08-Q06.text: Describe the puzzle pieces you can see. Use at least one number when you talk about them.

MA-SPK-T08-Q07.text: Look at the grapes. How would you describe them using a number? Say your sentence out loud.

MA-SPK-T08-Q08.text: There's a bunch of balloons on your screen. Tell me about them in your own words, and include a number.

MA-SPK-T08-Q09.text: A crowd of bees is buzzing on your screen. Can you describe them with a number? Say your sentence out loud.

MA-SPK-T08-Q10.text: Imagine you're a nature reporter. Describe the butterflies on your screen, and use a number in your report.

MA-SPK-T09-Q01.text: Look at the clock on your screen. Where are the hands pointing? Say the time out loud.

MA-SPK-T09-Q02.text: Here's a clock. Check the short hand and the long hand, then say what time it shows.

MA-SPK-T09-Q03.text: What time does this clock show? Take a careful look, then say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T09-Q04.text: Look closely at the clock face. When you've read the time, say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T09-Q05.text: Read the time on this clock. Check both hands before you decide, then say the time out loud.

MA-SPK-T09-Q06.text: This clock shows the time in digits. Say the time out loud, in words.

MA-SPK-T09-Q07.text: Have a look at the hands on this clock. What time is it? Say it clearly.

MA-SPK-T09-Q08.text: Here's a digital time. Can you say it out loud as a time in words? Take your time.

MA-SPK-T09-Q09.text: Tick tock. This clock shows a trickier time. Read the digits carefully and say the time out loud in words.

MA-SPK-T09-Q10.text: Here's another digital clock. Look at the hour and the minutes, then say the time out loud in words.

MA-SPK-T10-Q01.text: Here's a pattern: one, two, three, four. What's the rule that takes you from each number to the next? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q02.text: Look at this pattern: two, four, six, eight. What's happening each time? Say the rule out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q03.text: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. Can you spot the rule? Say it in your own words.

MA-SPK-T10-Q04.text: This pattern goes ten, nine, eight, seven. What rule is it following? Tell me out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q05.text: Time to be a pattern detective: three, six, nine, twelve. What's the rule? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q06.text: Look at the pattern: twenty, fifteen, ten, five. What rule gets you from each number to the next? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q07.text: One, three, five, seven. What do you notice? Say the rule for this pattern out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q08.text: Two, four, eight, sixteen. Look closely at how each number connects to the next, then say the rule out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q09.text: Here's a mystery pattern: one, one, two, three, five, eight. Can you crack the rule? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T10-Q10.text: Let's follow a number trail: one hundred, ninety, eighty, seventy. What rule keeps the trail going? Say it out loud.

MA-SPK-T11-Q01.text: You only need a quick look at these apples. Don't count them one by one; just say your best guess for how many there are.

MA-SPK-T11-Q02.text: Glance at the balloons, then say roughly how many you think there are. A sensible guess is all that's needed.

MA-SPK-T11-Q03.text: Take a quick peek at the coins. About how many are there? Say your best guess.

MA-SPK-T11-Q04.text: No counting this time. Look quickly at the fish and say about how many you think there are.

MA-SPK-T11-Q05.text: Have a fast look at the puzzle pieces. What's your estimate? Say a number that feels about right.

MA-SPK-T11-Q06.text: Think about walking from your bed to your front door. Roughly how many steps would that take? Say your best guess.

MA-SPK-T11-Q07.text: Picture yourself eating breakfast. About how many minutes does it take? Say your estimate out loud.

MA-SPK-T11-Q08.text: Whoosh, a crowd of butterflies. Look quickly and guess how many there are. Say your guess out loud.

MA-SPK-T11-Q09.text: Imagine your classroom filling up with people. Roughly how many could fit inside? Say your best guess.

MA-SPK-T11-Q10.text: Picture a small jar. If you filled it right up with coins, about how many do you think would fit? Say your guess out loud.

MA-SPK-T12-Q01.text: How would you work out four plus three? Talk me through your thinking, step by step.

MA-SPK-T12-Q02.text: Think about eight take away three. Explain out loud how you'd work it out, not just the answer.

MA-SPK-T12-Q03.text: How would you find double five? Describe the way you'd do it, in your own words.

MA-SPK-T12-Q04.text: Seven plus six. Explain your method out loud: what would you do first, and what next?

MA-SPK-T12-Q05.text: Imagine explaining fifteen minus eight to someone. How would you work it out? Talk through each step.

MA-SPK-T12-Q06.text: Think about three dogs. How would you work out how many legs they have in total? Explain your thinking out loud.

MA-SPK-T12-Q07.text: You have fifteen pence, and something costs twelve pence. How would you check whether you have enough? Explain your thinking.

MA-SPK-T12-Q08.text: Here's a bigger sum: twenty-seven plus fifteen. How would you tackle it? Tell me your plan, step by step.

MA-SPK-T12-Q09.text: Suppose you didn't know your times tables yet. How could you still work out three times four? Explain your idea out loud.

MA-SPK-T12-Q10.text: Halving an odd number like seven is a bit of a puzzle. How would you work it out? Talk through your thinking.

MA-SPK-T13-Q01.text: Listen carefully to the problem. First, tell it back in your own words. Then solve it and say your answer.

MA-SPK-T13-Q02.text: A short word problem is coming up. Listen all the way through, retell it your way, and then work out the answer.

MA-SPK-T13-Q03.text: Here comes a story with numbers in it. After you hear it, explain what happened in your own words, then solve it.

MA-SPK-T13-Q04.text: Listen to the problem closely. Can you say it again using your own words? Once you have, work out the answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T13-Q05.text: Pay attention to the numbers in this problem. Retell it in your own way first, and then give your solution.

MA-SPK-T13-Q06.text: Listen to the problem, then be the storyteller: say what's going on in your own words, and finish by solving it.

MA-SPK-T13-Q08.text: Get your listening ears ready for a story problem. Tell it back in your own words, then solve the puzzle out loud.

MA-SPK-T13-Q09.text: This story problem has a few parts, so listen right to the end. Retell it your way, then say what you think the answer is.

MA-SPK-T14-Q01.text: Listen to the problem. It has two steps, so work through them in order, then say your answer.

MA-SPK-T14-Q02.text: Here's a two-step problem. Listen carefully, solve the first step, then the second, and say what you get.

MA-SPK-T14-Q03.text: Two steps this time. Listen to the whole problem before you start, then say your final answer.

MA-SPK-T14-Q04.text: Listen closely: this problem has two parts. Keep track of what changes in each part, then say your answer.

MA-SPK-T14-Q05.text: This problem takes two steps. Listen, think it through, and say how many you end up with.

MA-SPK-T14-Q06.text: Listen to the problem and take it a step at a time. There are two steps. When you're done, say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T14-Q07.text: Get ready for a two-step problem. Listen carefully, work out each step, then tell me your answer.

MA-SPK-T14-Q08.text: A two-step puzzle is on its way. Listen right to the end, solve it bit by bit, and say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T14-Q09.text: Here's a challenge with bigger numbers and two steps. Listen carefully, work it out, then say your answer.

MA-SPK-T14-Q10.text: Listen to this two-step story. Follow what happens first and what happens next, then say your answer out loud.

MA-SPK-T15-Q01.text: Imagine a friend has never added two small numbers before. How would you teach them? Explain it out loud, step by step.

MA-SPK-T15-Q02.text: Pretend you're teaching a friend to count a group of objects without missing any. What tips would you give? Say them out loud.

MA-SPK-T15-Q03.text: A friend wants to know the difference between odd and even numbers. How would you explain it to them? Talk it through.

MA-SPK-T15-Q04.text: Your friend wants to know how to work out their change at a shop. How would you teach them? Explain it in your own words.

MA-SPK-T15-Q05.text: How would you teach a friend to tell if one number is bigger than another? Explain it in your own words.

MA-SPK-T15-Q06.text: Imagine helping a friend read a clock that shows an o'clock time. What would you tell them to look at? Explain out loud.

MA-SPK-T15-Q07.text: A friend needs to share some sweets fairly between two people. How would you show them what to do? Explain it out loud.

MA-SPK-T15-Q08.text: Two-step word problems can feel like a maze. How would you help a friend get through one without getting lost? Explain your tips.

MA-SPK-T15-Q09.text: Imagine you're the teacher today. How would you explain to a friend why checking your answer matters, even when you're pretty sure it's right?

MA-SPK-T15-Q10.text: Pretend you're explaining fractions to a friend. How do a half and a quarter connect to real sharing? Use an example you like, and talk it through.
